title: Resident Account Standing and the Home Purchase Financing Good-Faith Payment
content:
**Resident standing note — Home Purchase Financing good-faith payments**

A borrower's standing on the other accounts of the financed home's site bears on the good-faith payment. Where the borrower's Home-Site Lease for the financed home shows no rent owed and the Utility Pass-Through Service account of that same site shows no balance owed, the resident standing fraction is 0.5; where exactly one of the two shows nothing owed, the resident standing fraction is 0.75. Where both show an amount owed, no standing fraction applies.

"Shows no rent owed" and "shows no balance owed" mean a balance of zero or less on that account. The fraction applies to the good-faith payment amount before it is rounded, the payment being rounded half up to the cent once at the end.

| Home-Site Lease rent balance | Utility Pass-Through Service balance (same site) | Resident standing fraction |
|---|---|---|
| nothing owed | nothing owed | 0.5 |
| nothing owed | amount owed | 0.75 |
| amount owed | nothing owed | 0.75 |
| amount owed | amount owed | none applies |

### Questions the note answers

**Which lease counts?** The site lease of the financed home — the Home-Site Lease the loan is tied to — not any other lease the borrower may hold.

**Which utility account counts?** The Utility Pass-Through Service account of that same site.

**Hypothetical example.** An unrounded good-faith amount of 312.822, with rent fully paid but 48.20 owed on the site's utility account, becomes 312.822 times 0.75, that is 234.6165, which rounds to 234.62.
